title: Nettie Compton on the Pekin theater, club upstairs and stage stars
summary: Nettie and Simon Stewart performed upstairs; stars like Charles Gilpin and Florence Mills passed through the theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Simon Stewart and me, there was no band. Simon played and I sang.
Was that upstairs, Mrs. Compton? Yes.
Almost the whole space of the theater.
No, during the theater. I saw the theater, came upstairs.
Oh, I see. You had the club upstairs.
I worked on the stage and would go upstairs.

I saw that place after it was a police station. Yeah. The policemen took me around, showed me some room upstairs. They said it had been the club. But downstairs they had the Black Mariah there where the stage used to be. That old, that was 27th Street, wasn't it? Yeah, 27th Street.
Showed me that years ago. Gee, that was a great theater then.
Isn't that where Shelton Brooks wrote? Yeah, some of these days. I believe somebody told me that some of the most famous actors and dancers that Bill Robinson used to wear. Oh, yes.
All the great stars of the stage used to come there.
Charlie Gilpin played Emperor Jones. Oh, yes.
Charlie Gilpin. Yeah, we worked there. We were in the same stuff company. You were in the same company.

Just past his room there on the right, coming in. Gilpin. On the left going out. He lived with us. He lived there. He lived there. When he went to Milwaukee, we went up there on a visit with him when he played Emperor Jones up there.
Yeah, those were some great times.
There was Florence Mills as a room too. That's Florence's picture up there.
